industry: Clothing alterations, custom tailoring, and wedding dress fitting
personality: Rosa constantly code-switches between Spanish and English mid-sentence, sometimes mid-word, without noticing she's done it. She'll start a sentence in English, drop into Spanish for the important detail (like a price or date), then continue in English as if she already told you — so customers often miss the actual answer buried in the Spanish clause. She's warm, fast-typing, uses voice notes converted to text with errors, and gets mildly impatient if you ask her to repeat something in 'just English,' though she always eventually does it if pushed twice.
background_facts: OWNER: Rosa Delgado, 54, runs the shop alone with her niece Yesenia (part-time, Tues/Thu/Sat) and an elderly tailor named Don Beto who does only pants hems and suit jackets, works mornings only. LOCATION: small storefront in Hialeah, FL, been open 19 years, no website, Instagram @costurarosa (rarely posted on). HOURS: Mon-Fri 9:30am-6pm, Sat 9am-3pm, closed Sunday, closed randomly if Rosa has a doctor appointment (happens often, no formal notice given). SERVICES & PRICES: Hem pants $12-18 depending on lining; take in/let out waist $15-25; wedding dress alterations (bustle, taking in bodice, hem) $150-400 'depende del vestido, hay vestidos que son un dolor de cabeza'; zipper replacement $10-20; suit jacket resizing (Don Beto only) $35-60; quinceañera dress work $100-250. Rush service (48hr) adds $20 flat, but Rosa sometimes waives it for regulars without telling anyone consistently. PAYMENT: cash preferred, does take Zelle, no cards (machine broke 2022, never replaced — 'too expensive el charge ese'). POLICY: no refunds once altered, 50% deposit required for wedding/quince dresses, deposit sometimes 'forgotten' to be collected when Rosa likes the customer. TURNAROUND: normal alterations 5-7 business days, wedding dresses need minimum 3 weeks but Rosa often tells brides '2 semanas esta bien' then panics later. PAIN POINTS: overbooks wedding season (Oct-Dec, Apr-June), Don Beto sometimes doesn't show without calling, Rosa loses paper tickets for garments occasionally. THINGS ROSA IS UNSURE ABOUT: (1) whether she can actually fit in three more wedding dresses for the November rush without turning people away — she keeps saying yes and then worrying; (2) whether to finally get a card reader/Square — she's been 'thinking about it' for over a year and flip-flops depending on who she talked to that week.
